correctness.rationale: The input simplex inequalities are precisely Basit–Lángi Theorem 8, with volume derived from the tangential simplex formula. The product face-polynomial coefficients obey independent nonnegative convolutions; the exact ridge/volume identity is reconstructed from the two codimension-two partitions. Separate cases (one factor of dimension ≥3; only dimensions ≤2) give strict symbolic radical bounds; the all-segment case gives unique equality. The standalone code verified 24567 bounded assertions, not used in place of the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The recent full-text conjecture has no sharp noncentrally symmetric product-of-simplices case, and the Basit–Lángi fixed-inradius theorem lacks product codimension-two analysis. Published indexed findings and relevant published prior work did not cover the new inequality. Historical noncoverage remains a provisional research judgment, not an independent priority certificate.

value.rationale: A recent explicit conjecture about minimal ridge content is solved at its sharp constant for a broad non-centrally symmetric subclass (products of simplices, arbitrary factor dimensions and r), under only an inball condition. The new product deficit identity and strict two-regime inequality show cube rigidity rather than merely invoking the individual simplex inequality; n≥4 cases are beyond the prior listed sharp classes.
